document.job: PM turns the Wikipedia OKR article into a multi-plate briefing, then rewrites the title.
document.title: Objectives and key results
document.lead: Framework used to define measurable goals and their outcomes. OKR is a goal-setting framework used by individuals, teams, and organizations to define measurable goals and track their outcomes.
document.about: The development of OKR is generally attributed to Andrew Grove who introduced the approach to Intel in the 1970s and documented the framework in his 1983 book High Output Management.
document.skills:
• John Doerr introduced OKRs to Google in 1999 after learning iMBOs at Intel.
  • Doerr published Measure What Matters in 2018.
  • Larry Page credited OKRs with 10× growth at Alphabet.
document.principles:
• Target about 70% success on aspirational key results.
  • Score on a 0.0 to 1.0 scale; 1.0 is expected for committed results.
  • Avoid business-as-usual wording such as help or consult.
